newsitem.title: USA: Chinese delegation visits U.S. for TCK smut tour.
newsitem.headline: Chinese delegation visits U.S. for TCK smut tour.

text.p: A U.S. agriculture official said Thursday he was hopeful of progress in the current round of discussions with China on the issue of TCK smut fungus in U.S. wheat.
Agriculture Department General Sales Manager Chris Goldthwait said a team of Chinese experts was currently viewing U.S. wheat producing areas and Gulf export points.
"We believe the Chinese side is approaching this visit with a positive attitude, as are we," Goldthwait told USDA radio.
Goldthwait, who met the team in Denver recently, said he was hopeful of some progress but added that there were no guarantees.

China has for years refused to buy wheat from the U.S. Pacific Northwest because of tilletia controversa kuhn (TCK) smut, and earlier this year cancelled shipments from U.S. Gulf points for the same reason.
Goldthwait said USDA did not have a complete understanding of why TCK showed up in wheat shipped from the Gulf.
He said the United States did not regard the disease, which has no human health effects, as a serious problem, except in trade with China.
